basics.title:
A residency inside a
working community
body:
Field Station is a Logos residency that places builders inside a
real parallel community for eight days. Residents live where
they build, and each project starts from a local problem.

The first Field Station took place at Dhun, a 500-acre
regenerative project in Rajasthan's Jaipur district, run with
ZuGrama.

Residents shared meals, walks, and morning rituals. They held
sessions on everything from breath work to AI safety, enjoyed
impromptu cricket games and music evenings, and shared in
meal preparation and hosting. Each day had its own programme
of resident-curated activities, as well as a four-hour build cycle.

On the first day, Dhun's founder, Manvendra Singh Shekhawat,
asked the residents to build tools that solve local and national
challenges.

image.alt: Residents talking together outdoors at Dhun at night

basics.label: The Dhun residency ran four tracks:

tracks.title: The Logos Civic Prize
tracks.body:
Tools to rebuild civil society, set against two
prizes defined by Logos Circles: civic
reporting and community response, and
privacy-preserving mutual aid.

tracks.title:
Sovereignty and
Privacy
tracks.body:
Private-by-default tools that let people and
communities hold their own money, data and
records, built on the Logos stack.

tracks.title: d/acc, led by ZuGrama
tracks.body:
Decentralised acceleration across AI,
neurotech, and bio-resilience, meeting the
Logos stack where AI, cryptography, and
sovereignty overlap.

tracks.title: Residents
tracks.body:
For organisers, artists, writers, and testers
who joined to use the tools as they were built,
rather than to ship code.

community.title:
Technology built through
community
body:
Logos is a technology stack and a social movement that
develop together. The parallel communities putting private,
peer-to-peer technology to work also shape the design of the
tools comprising the stack.

Field Station aligns both privacy-preserving technology and the
movement for parallel societies.
community.statement:
At Dhun, residents designed
for households, farms, and
the village as a whole.
details:
Living on the land, sharing meals, and measuring their output
against the needs of a regenerative community, residents at
Dhun came from across India.

Meals were long and phone-free, people walked everywhere,
and evenings meant horse rides and cricket on the lawn, played
badly and with great enthusiasm.

projects.title: What the residents built
projects.body:
Four winners were chosen from the 23 applications developed
at the residency. These are early proof-of-concept tools running
on test networks.
projects.disclaimer:
These tools are shared for informational purposes. Code is not reviewed
by Logos and may contain bugs, change without notice, or behave
unexpectedly.

entries.title: Offline Zcash
entries.lead:
Offline Zcash is an open-source wallet and mesh
network for Basecamp that sends private Zcash
payments without an internet connection.
entries.body:
The wallet signs a payment on the device. Nearby devices pass the
sealed payment along until it reaches the payee, and a gateway with
internet access settles it on Zcash later. The devices relaying it
cannot read it.

entries.title: Bosphorus
entries.lead:
Bosphorus is a wallet and lending app that runs inside
Logos Basecamp. A user moves funds from a public
account into a private one then borrows against
collateral.
entries.body:
The app proves the loan is safely collateralised without revealing
who it belongs to. Bosphorus covers the credit link of the chain,
agreeing a loan and settling it while the borrower's position stays
private.

image.alt: Bosphorus private lending application in Logos Basecamp

entries.title: Pukaar
entries.lead:
Pukaar is a decentralised community issue tracker that
runs in Basecamp.
entries.body:
Residents log faults and follow each one until it is fixed. A steward
can mark a fix as done, but it is only confirmed once the person who
reported it, or two other residents, confirm it. The person who
reported the issue can reopen it at any time.

image.alt: Aditya demonstrating Pukaar at the residency

entries.title: Dhun Commons
entries.lead:
Dhun Commons is a wallet and coordination space for
the farmers and stewards of Dhun's 500 acres, running
in Basecamp.
entries.body:
Each season has one treasury, shared by three parties, and every
release of funds needs two signatures. When a milestone is reached,
the treasury releases on quorum, with eight percent going to
conservation. A field map, advisories, and a coordination room keep
evidence for each decision, served through Logos Storage.

image.alt: Dhun Commons treasury and coordination application
Residents gathered outdoors at Dhun at night

quotes.quote:
"Culture can be something we consciously experiment with.
With Fieldstation and the technological freedoms enabled by
Logos, we have an opportunity to explore this in practice. At
ZuGrama, we are building a permanent node to put this
into a long-term experiment."

"Field Station brought some wonderfully curious
people to Dhun. The range of their pursuits and the
conviction behind them sparked our imagination.
My team and I are keen to see what we might build together."

modules.title: Built on Logos
body:
The Logos tech stack lays the groundwork for peer-to-peer
applications built for parallel societies.

The winning projects use the Logos stack for jobs a village
would otherwise hand to a central server, demonstrating the
real-world utility of tools built for parallel systems.

entries.title: Logos Delivery
entries.body:
Logos peer-to-peer data transport protocols carry the coordination: reports,
confirmations, and approvals pass directly between residents' devices, encrypted to
the people taking part without needing a middleman.

entries.title: Logos Storage
entries.body:
Logos Storage allows users to privately serve and retrieve files between each other
themselves without needing to hand custody to a third party.

entries.title: Logos Execution Zone
entries.body:
The Logos execution stack supports elective privacy, allowing users to choose when
and how their value transfers are kept hidden while also enabling public transparency
where it is needed.

architecture.title: Local-first on Basecamp
body:
Logos Basecamp is a local-first launcher for peer-to-peer apps
built on Logos. It loads each app and the modules it needs on
your own machine, with no hosted frontend and no sign-up.

Each winning tool from the Field Station uses Basecamp to
remove dependence on a company's server, allowing users to
hold their own data.

features.title: Run on Basecamp
features.body:
Bosphorus, Pukaar, Offline Zcash, and Dhun Commons run as
apps or modules inside Basecamp.

features.title: No central server
features.body:
Using Logos tools provided through Basecamp, these
applications do not rely on servers. They are peer-to-peer.

closing.body:
Field Station shows what happens when a technology stack
built for parallel societies meets a movement with local
problems in mind.
closing.disclaimer:
Field Station / Rajasthan was a Logos residency run with ZuGrama at Dhun. All
projects shown are prototypes built by independent residents. None has been
audited. They run on test networks, and none should be used with real money.
